Tech Report: How to use your phone if the grid goes down

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down? Power and tech outages continue to cause disruptions, and that can leave you stuck when it comes to staying in touch with others.

Sources indicate that there are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it. You’ll need to make sure the people you’re chatting with have set up the same options, so it’s worth mentioning at the next family or friends gathering.

Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.

If you’ve acquired a phone from Apple, Samsung, or Google in the last two or three years, it comes with satellite communications built in, so you can still text friends and family if the cell towers go out (calling isn’t an option, due to bandwidth). The feature should kick in automatically in Messages on iOS, or in Google Messages on Android, provided your carrier supports it—you’ll just see a prompt on screen.

Follow the instructions to find a satellite and start texting. There’s nothing to enable or turn on, but if you want to test it out beforehand so you know it works, open Settings, then pick Apps > Messages > Satellite Connection Demo (iOS), or Safety and emergency > Satellite SOS (Android).

According to recent reports, there is another option on your phone, which is to try a peer-to-peer messaging app. These apps need to be downloaded in advance and work over Bluetooth to send messages in a mesh created by the devices themselves. That means a limited range, but you don’t need any Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.

One of the best apps in this category is Bridgefy, which you can get for Android and iOS. It’s free to use, simple to operate, and has a range of around 100 meters (or 330 feet). You don’t have to wait until the power goes out to use it either, because you could set up a mesh chat when you’re out camping or taking a trip with family.

It has been revealed that unless you do a lot of outdoor, off-grid adventuring, you might not have realized just how many devices now exist that can keep you connected even without access to Wi-Fi or cellular networks. Some of these options work via the same satellite networks as your phone.

According to recent reports, have a look at the Garmin InReach Messenger Plus, for example, a $299.99 communicator you can use whenever cell networks are down (or just out of range). You’re also going to need an active subscription. They start at $7.99 a month, but once you’re set up you can connect to the wider world from just about anywhere.

Then there are the more straightforward walkie-talkie devices, which operate over radio signals across a range of a few miles. That might just be enough if you’ve got friends and family you need to contact when the power’s out. There are plenty of devices to choose between, but the Motorola T802 Talkabout is a good example and under $100 for a pair.

Don’t forget a battery-powered radio either. It won’t let you message anyone directly, but it will mean you can stay up to date with what’s happening out there in the world, and it might give you an idea of when the power’s going to come back on. You can even get models that work via solar or hand-crank power, like this $30 emergency radio.

All of your phones and other devices will need power if they’re going to keep you in touch with other people—otherwise you’ll be relying on smoke signals and postal couriers. So it’s wise to invest in a portable power station ahead of time. Something like the $289 Jackery Explorer 300 would do the job.

Industry observers note that obviously, you’re going to want to charge up these hefty power stations before the electricity gets cut, otherwise they won’t be much use. But you’re actually not as reliant on the power grid as you might think. Many models (including those offered by Jackery) have solar panel add-ons you can invest in as well.

It has been revealed that even with a backup supply in place, it’s a good idea to try and conserve power on your gadgets as much as possible too. Your phones, tablets, and laptops will all have low power settings you can make use of, but there are standard tips that apply across just about every gadget. Reduce screen brightness and volume as much as possible, and enable airplane mode where you can.

Recent findings suggest that when you do have power and Wi-Fi available, make sure you download as much essential info to your phone as you can, so it’s still there when an internet connection isn’t. This is particularly useful for maps: Both Google Maps (Settings > Offline maps) and Apple Maps (Profile picture > Offline maps) let you do this.

The Failure Rate of Public Schools Is a Tragedy

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.

In a recent development, as described in the article “In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own?,” teenager Najya Hannah-Jones confronted her mother, the prominent journalist Nikole Hannah-Jones, about the choice to send her to public school in a system that, for many, provides substandard education. It was refreshing to read of Najya fighting to get a better education, a striking contrast with the popular but often inaccurate stereotype of lazy teens aiming to learn as little as possible. More importantly, kudos to Nikole Hannah-Jones for candidly admitting in her article that teachers lied to her about what they were teaching and, worse, tried to deceive both mother and daughter about what had actually been learned.

Every parent has a duty to nurture their children, but all parents also must consider their values when choosing schools for their children, so it is heartbreaking to realize that Ms. Hannah-Jones could have chosen a far better public school in New York for her daughter that would have met the core values listed in her article. Public school? Check. Racially diverse or perhaps even predominately Black student body? Check. Most importantly, a track record of meeting educational standards and being honest with parents regarding what their child is learning and how they are performing? Check and check.

It has been revealed that the truth is that Nikole Hannah-Jones could have enrolled her daughter in a local public school where the majority of students are Black and other nonwhite families and has long offered much better odds for positive educational outcomes. There has long been such an option available to parents that is too often ignored: New York City charter schools.

In the book Charter Schools and Their Enemies, Thomas Sowell painstakingly and convincingly reveals that public charter schools in Fresh York City consistently outperform neighborhood schools. Based on Ms. Hannah-Jones essay, one could argue that is not an especially high bar, but the data in the book show academic superiority relative to even the higher-quality schools in New York City, New York State, and nationwide. It is noteworthy that Sowell meticulously controls for the usual “straw men” used to assault charter schools. Indeed, some of the charter schools were not only in the same neighborhoods, but in the same building as the comparison schools in his study.

According to recent reports, it is an ongoing tragedy that Ms. Hannah-Jones and others in the Black community are not demanding an expansion of public charter school options for their children. After all, and perhaps this is why they are under assault, public charter schools provide prima facia evidence that Newly introduced York can, in fact, deliver a high-quality public education, but chooses not to do so. One hopes that other families like the Hannah-Joneses will enroll their children in public charter schools and demand that New York City be more honest what is being taught and what their children have learned.

Industry observers note that the national discussion Ms. Hannah-Jones has sparked has been overwhelmingly focused on schools with majority Black student enrollment, but the debate should not be narrowly circumscribed. The truth is that every teen enrolled in failing schools across the U.S. should be asking their parents the same question Najya Hannah-Jones asked her mother: Why are you sending me to a school you already know is delivering a substandard education?

Recent findings suggest that stripped to essentials, Ms. Hannah-Jones faced the same choice most families do when deciding whether to enroll their children in public schools, regardless of race: If I send my child to the local school as a kindergartner, what is the probability that my child will emerge from 8th grade with the basic reading and math skills needed to succeed in high school and beyond? It turns out that there are ample data to help parents answer this question.

The National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP) provides annual statistics on U.S. education outcomes. Nationally, only 26% of 8th-graders are proficient or above in math, according to its 2022 Nation's Report Card; only about one in four children are entering high school with grade-level proficiency in math. Reading outcomes are only slightly better, with 28% of 8th-graders being rated as proficient. Candidly, this is a national disgrace that poses an excruciating dilemma for parents and students.

According to recent reports, A usual response to this data is to argue that public schools are underfunded. New York spends an average of more than $30,000 per student. Overall, the U.S. consistently spends more per pupil than nearly every other country in the world, including many that deliver better outcomes while paying less than half of what the U.S spends. More money is not translating to better outcomes. Does anyone believe that even doubling expenditures or even tripling them would appreciably improve outcomes at the school Najya Hannah-Jones attended, or any other failing school? After all, real spending, even adjusted for inflation, has more than doubled in the past 25 years and outcomes are actually a bit worse nationwide over the same period.

If it is not simply spending more money, what should parents do? The best answer: Do your homework. There are often options. Many states have adopted public options, including public charter schools, public magnet schools, and other similar approaches.

According to recent reports, several of my own children attended a public school implementing a Montessori teaching approach and two of my granddaughters are currently enrolled in a similar public school in Nashville. I was (and am) very pleased with what they were taught, how they were taught, and what they learned. Another daughter attended an academic magnet public high school that consistently outperforms even the most expensive private schools, even though, in general, Nashville public schools often have relatively poor outcomes for most students. The evidence is overwhelming that public school systems know how to deliver a high-quality education. Why are they choosing not to? Najya Hannah-Jones is absolutely right to demand answers and all teens—and their parents—should be asking the same questions.

Sources indicate that sowell, T. (2020). Charter schools and their enemies. Basic Books.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Road & Track just returned from our fifth Hudson Quattrocento rally, and this year’s festivities were a familiar reminder of why we can’t stay away from Upstate New York.
  • Drivers indicated out with a diverse lineup of cars: a 2026 Bentley Continental GTC Speed, a 2000 Ferrari 456M GT, a 2026 Lotus Emira, and even a Cinnabar Red 1988 BMW M6.
  • Day one of Hudson Quattrocento kicked off at Scribner’s Catskill Lodge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Road & Track just returned from our fifth Hudson Quattrocento rally, and this year’s festivities were a familiar reminder of why we can’t stay away from Upstate New York. A special group of readers from across the United States and Canada spent four days driving through the Hudson Valley and Catskill Mountains, touring the greatest roads from past rallies and exploring some all-new pavement, too. Fun fact: the “quattrocento” in the rally’s namesake comes from the Italian word for “four hundred”, alluding to the four-hundred-mile route of our first-ever Hudson Quattrocento rally. This year, we gave participants an extra 80 miles, plus a couple of surprises along the way.

Drivers indicated out with a diverse lineup of cars: a 2026 Bentley Continental GTC Speed, a 2000 Ferrari 456M GT, a 2026 Lotus Emira, and even a Cinnabar Red 1988 BMW M6. The drive was led by Editor-in-Chief Dan Pund in an Aston Martin Vanquish Volante, Editor-at-Large Matt Farah in a Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC, and Executive Editor Mike Austin in a Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing. Our official event partner, Corient, also came along for the ride to help make Hudson Quattrocento an unforgettable rally.

Day one of Hudson Quattrocento kicked off at Scribner’s Catskill Lodge. Guests checked in at registration, grabbed a light bite, got briefed on the rally’s road rules, and listened to introductions from Road & Track staff and fellow attendees.

Rally participants lined up in their driving groups for the first route—an out-and-back joyride to Rhinebeck, NY. Peak autumn offers a magical driving experience in the Hudson Valley, with winding roads lined with bursts of red, orange, and yellow leaves and the crisp sting of not-yet-cold fall air.

In Rhinebeck, we stopped for lunch at Gigi Trattoria and afforded guests time to explore the charming Hudson Valley town. We hopped back in our cars and completed the loop back to Scribner’s Catskill Lodge, where guests checked into their rooms and explored the woodsy property.

Industry observers note that after a little downtime, we gathered for drinks and dinner in the Apex Lounge. Later, we took full advantage of being in the chilly mountains by gathering around a cozy firepit and enjoying s’mores. Guests then tucked in for the night and rested up for the following day’s track activities.

Guests started Day Two with breakfast at the hotel before lining up in our driving groups. The group headed west to Wilzig Racing Manor, a private, Grand Prix-style racing circuit in entrepreneur and semi-pro driver Alan Wilzig’s backyard. This exclusive track is not typically open to the public, so getting a turn at the 1.1-mile road course was a real privilege. After lapping the elevation-heavy road course, we also got the chance to explore Wilzig’s unreal collection of classic cars, race cars, and motorcycles. From the 2006 Ariel Atom and 2008 Lotus 2-Eleven to the 2017 Ginetta LMP3 or 1974 Ducati Sport, we had enough automotive eye candy to keep us busy for a while.

We left Wilzig Racing Manor and pointed west on Highway 28A until we found some twisty back roads. 98 miles later, we pulled into Callicoon Center, NY, and arrived at Callicoon Hills Resort. Attendees were greeted with a lavish charcuterie board and a bottle of wine in their rooms, courtesy of Corient. The evening concluded with drinks and dinner at Callicoon Hills’ rustic Prospect Restaurant. After dinner, guests retired to their rooms to rest up for our second track day.

Miles logged: 130.8 (plus several more laps around the track).

According to recent reports, after fueling up with breakfast at the hotel, we rallied to Lime Rock Park for our second track day of the trip. Drivers tracked their cars on Lime Rock Park’s historic seven-turn, 1.5-mile road course. Three-time 24 Hours of Daytona champion and former IndyCar driver Ryan Briscoe also joined us, giving guests hot laps in a Spec Miata. After mastering the track, we amped up the friendly competition with a timed autocross competition. Guests zipped, weaved, and bobbed through a couple hundred cones for the chance to win a coveted Hudson Quattrocento award. (More to be revealed soon…).

Recent findings suggest that we then continued our journey with a short ten-mile drive to Troutbeck Hotel in Amenia, NY—something we were grateful for after giving it our all at the track. Upon arrival, guests settled into their rooms and enjoyed the beautiful grounds.

Industry observers note that before dinner, we gathered in the hotel’s library for an intimate fireside chat between Dan Pund and Briscoe. We rounded out the night with the Hudson Quattrocento award ceremony featuring awards for the Fastest Time, Driver of the Day, Longest Drive, and Best Co-Pilot, presented by Corient.

Miles logged: 138.9 (plus several more laps around the track).

We queued up in our driving groups for one last time as we headed east for the rally’s final stop in Portland, CT. TV personality and master car restorer Wayne Carini gave us a private tour of his personal garage and car collection.

As guests enjoyed their wood-fired pizza lunch, Matt Farah sat down with Carini for a fireside chat about his career, collection, and upcoming projects. Afterward, Carini signed copies of his book Steering Through Life.

In a recent development, guests exchanged hugs and contact information and mentioned final goodbyes as the rally concluded. Hudson Quattrocento was an unforgettable rally—complete with stunning drives, multiple track days, thrilling pit stops, and fantastic tech giant.

Sources indicate that if you would like to get in on the action yourself, there are plenty of opportunities to hit the road with us in 2027. We’re heading to Southern California on February 23-26 for Palm Canyon Run, then heading to Upcoming Hampshire, Maine, and Vermont for New England Run on May 17-20. We hope to see you there!

Industry News: Energy Drinks, Stimulant Supplements Linked to Higher Heart Risks in Young Adults

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1374 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.
  • The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.
  • Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.

The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.

Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.

“These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk,” study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, VA, stated in a news release.

“For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can quickly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it’s crucial for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products,” Samayamanthula continued.

Researchers from the University of Virginia School of Medicine analyzed 28,345 reports submitted to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) between 2017 and 2025.

Of these, 854 involved caffeinated energy drinks or stimulant supplements, while the remaining reports involved non-stimulant products.

Compared with non-stimulant products, cardiac arrest was reported approximately 11 times more often with energy drinks and stimulant supplements. Heart attacks were reported 4.5 times more often, while ventricular arrhythmias and palpitations were reported about four times more frequently.

Nearly 45% of heart-related reports involved adults ages 18 to 34.

It has been revealed that “Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products,” Samayamanthula remarked.

Gregory M. Marcus, MD, professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine, and chair of the 2026 AHA scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease, wasn’t involved in the study, but mentioned the research “raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system.”.

“Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis,” Marcus mentioned in a news release.

“More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.”.

Industry observers note that cheng-Han Chen, MD, board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA, noted the findings, although concerning, are not surprising. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“We know that energy drinks can have significant effects on the cardiovascular system, primarily because of their stimulant properties,” he told Healthline.

Sources indicate that “Caffeine can increase blood pressure and heart rate, while other ingredients, such as guarana and taurine, may further contribute to cardiovascular stimulation and increased stress hormone levels. What is particularly concerning is the potential for these products to trigger serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms, especially in people with underlying cardiovascular conditions.”.

Sources indicate that chen agreed that occasional energy drink consumption is unlikely to have long-term consequences for heart health in most healthy individuals. However, he stated that “frequent or excessive consumption can potentially increase the risk of hypertension and cardiac arrhythmias.”.

It has been revealed that an AHA scientific statement published in July 2026 notes that up to 400 milligrams of caffeine daily is generally considered safe for most healthy adults. That’s roughly equivalent to four or five 8-ounce cups of brewed coffee, depending on how it’s prepared.

However, some energy drinks contain up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee.

Certain energy drinks may also contain stimulants, such as guarana, yerba mate, theobromine, synephrine, and yohimbine.

These ingredients may compound caffeine’s effects on the cardiovascular system.

“Caffeine stimulates the cardiovascular system, primarily by increasing sympathetic nervous system activity. This can cause the heart to beat faster, raise blood pressure, and increase the workload on the heart,” Chen remarked.

“Energy drinks may contain additional stimulants, such as guarana and taurine, which can further increase blood pressure and stress hormone levels. With excessive consumption, these effects can become more pronounced and potentially interfere with the heart’s normal electrical activity, increasing the risk of abnormal heart rhythms. People with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly hypertension or a predisposition to arrhythmias, may be especially vulnerable to these effects.”.

Other research has echoed these concerns. A 2025 review suggests that high-volume energy drink consumption can prolong the heart’s QTc interval, increase blood pressure, and raise heart rate beyond the effects of caffeine alone.

“There is growing concern about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements, particularly among younger adults,” Chen said.

“One challenge is that younger individuals may not recognize that these products can have significant effects on their heart and blood pressure, especially when consumed frequently or in combination with other caffeinated products.”.

Young adults accounted for a substantial portion of the FDA reports included in the study, highlighting potential cardiovascular concerns for this age group.

People with existing heart conditions, a history of irregular heart rhythms, or heightened caffeine sensitivity may face additional risks. Those with undiagnosed genetic heart conditions may also be vulnerable.

A 2024 study identified cases of sudden cardiac arrest occurring shortly after energy drink consumption, particularly among people with underlying inherited heart conditions.

“As a cardiologist, I am particularly concerned about people who may have underlying cardiovascular conditions that have not yet been diagnosed,” Chen said.

It has been revealed that “Excessive stimulant intake can potentially trigger symptoms such as palpitations, chest discomfort, and lightheadedness. In susceptible individuals, it may also increase the risk of more serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms.”.

Additionally, combining energy drinks with strenuous exercise or alcohol may introduce additional cardiovascular risks.

The findings suggest an association between energy drinks, stimulant supplements, and reported cardiovascular events, but they are preliminary and do not establish cause and effect.

The FDA database also relied on voluntary adverse-event reports, meaning some events may never be reported, while others may receive disproportionate attention.

Researchers also do not yet know how many people consumed these products without experiencing any problems. Without this variable, the reports cannot establish actual risk.

Recent findings suggest that other factors, including underlying health conditions, medications, and lifestyle habits, may also influence the results. More systematic research and controlled clinical trials are needed.

For most healthy adults, consuming up to 400 milligrams of caffeine per day is generally considered safe.

However, Chen noted that individual tolerance for caffeine may vary, and people with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly high blood pressure or abnormal heart rhythms, may need to limit or avoid caffeine altogether.

“Energy drinks can vary considerably in their caffeine content and serving sizes,” Chen remarked.

It has been revealed that “Depending on the product, a single can may contain anywhere from 80 to 300 milligrams of caffeine. This means that consuming even one or two energy drinks can put someone close to or above the recommended daily limit, particularly when combined with coffee, tea, or other caffeinated supplements.”.

Seek emergency medical attention if you experience chest pain, particularly if it’s accompanied by shortness of breath, fainting, or other symptoms of a possible heart attack.

If you live with a heart condition, ask your doctor about your daily caffeine intake to determine whether you need to cut back.

“Depending on the severity of these symptoms, medical attention may be necessary,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that still, most people may not need to give up caffeine entirely. Monitoring your habits could help protect your heart health. This may include:.

Industry observers note that “I encourage people to read product labels carefully and be aware of their total daily caffeine consumption,” Chen said. “I particularly recommend that people with underlying cardiovascular conditions avoid energy drinks.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Boston’s New England Aquarium recently shipped a very important package.
  • “By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the New England Aquarium, tells Popular Science.
  • Sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boston’s New England Aquarium recently shipped a very important package. But it wasn’t exactly an early Christmas gift. The team shipped 22 lookdown fish across the country via air transport. And they’re not the only institution that routinely packs fishes up and sends them elsewhere. The NEA are part of a group of aquariums where each member specializes in raising certain species on behalf of the entire group. They then send the fish to the other member aquariums.

“By working together, we are able to raise more fish, and develop aquaculture practices to successfully raise more species, including some that have never been raised before, like copper/glassy sweepers, blue chromis, and brown chromis,” Monika Schmück, manager of sustainability in the fishes department at the New England Aquarium, tells Popular Science. “We typically raise 500-1000 fish annually and distribute them to over 15 institutions on average each year.”.

Sharing is caring, even amongst aquariums. When it comes time for the fish’s journey, the team needs to decide whether to use air or ground transport. To do this, they consider factors including external temperature, the weight of the shipment, and access to an airport at the destination. Depending on the time of the year, cargo holding and ground transport trucks can experience extreme temperatures, Schmück points out.

Recent findings suggest that if it’s a large shipment, the New England Aquarium usually goes for air cargo, whereas smaller shipments are easier to deliver with ground transportation. Overall, ground transportation is the easiest strategy because it doesn’t have to take into account the location of airports.

On a smaller scale, moving a fish isn’t as easy as sticking a cat into a crate. In terms of the container in which the animal will travel, the biggest consideration is the size of noted animal, which determines how much water it needs.

“Since fish must be transported in water, and water is heavy, the design of a fish transport first must address how to safely move the required volume of water to keep the fish safe and secure during the process,” Schmück explains.

Ultimately, the fundamentals of fish transport are mostly consistent no matter the species. Experts need to make sure that the water chemistry is good during the entire trip and that other environmental conditions are appropriate for the traveling species and remain stable.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

According to recent reports, november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Sources indicate that given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A first-of-its-kind international food pyramid, developed by 22 leading nutritionists from Europe, Canada, the United States, and Australia, was published in Advances in Nutrition in September.

This newly introduced food pyramid emphasizes plant-based protein sources, cooking with plant-based oils, and healthier sugars and carbohydrates.

It also echoes the traditional food pyramid used in the United States since 1992.

Industry observers note that the latest pyramid breaks away from the Trump administration’s updated nutritional guidelines, which are part of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Health Again (MAHA) agenda and prioritize red meat over plants.

Industry observers note that the latest pyramid was designed by a research team led by Brigham Young University professor Karen Della Corte. The researchers noted that this is the first international food pyramid that is designed to reflect scientific agreement across multiple countries and cultures.

Della Corte and researchers from the International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC), compared dietary guidelines from multiple countries, including:.

They also analyzed evidence from more than 250 scientific publications, while drawing on the EAT-Lancet Planetary Health Diet to identify principles of healthy eating that may be shared.

The new pyramid highlights three guidelines:.

While the pyramid emphasizes plant-based proteins, it doesn’t exclude animal proteins.

“I find the fresh international food pyramid a more practical and aligned approach for the prevention of chronic disease,” stated Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the creation of the food pyramid.

“The latest international food pyramid places greater emphasis on food quality and the importance of building meals around nutrient-dense plant foods, while still allowing room for lean animal proteins such as fish, poultry, eggs, and yogurt,” she added.

While the new pyramid and the current U.S. dietary guidelines differ in many ways, they also agree on certain factors.

For example, both sets of guidelines discourage added sugars, refined carbs, and highly processed snacks.

In a recent development, the differences between the two mainly lie in their emphasis on specific sources of protein and fat. For example, the new pyramid prioritizes plant-based proteins, while the U.S. guidelines place greater emphasis on animal proteins, including red meat.

Industry observers note that while both sets of recommendations advise limiting saturated fat, the upcoming pyramid emphasizes unsaturated plant oils, whereas the U.S. guidelines also include butter and beef tallow as cooking fat options.

Industry observers note that routhenstein noted that an key distinction is that this new pyramid goes beyond simply telling people to eat more protein or fewer carbohydrates. Instead, it encourages people to consider the quality and sources of those nutrients.

However, the main emphasis of both guidelines is encouraging people to eat fewer ultra-processed foods and more natural or “real” foods.

Routhenstein told Healthline that research consistently indicates that plant-forward eating patterns, including the Mediterranean and DASH diets, are associated with better cardiovascular health and a lower risk of heart disease.

Plant foods provide fiber, potassium, antioxidants, and other beneficial compounds that can help support healthy cholesterol levels, blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood vessel function.

“This is not to say that protein and fat are unimportant, but their sources matter,” Routhenstein said.

In a statement from BYU, Della Corte shared the following tips for incorporating the new pyramid’s recommendations into your diet:.

Industry observers note that the pyramid is a framework, not a personalized prescription. If you have questions about your individual nutritional needs, you can speak with your healthcare professional or a licensed dietitian.

“It is crucial to recognize that plant-forward does not mean vegan or vegetarian. The amount and sources of animal protein should be considered to ensure they align with an individual’s cardiometabolic goals and lab targets,” Routhenstein said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles.
  • It has been revealed that despite the growing recall population, the core matter remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that 18 years after Honda filed the first official airbag recall and 12 years since the first round of mass recalls began, the Takata airbag scandal remains ongoing. This month, Honda and Toyota have both filed fresh recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration related to faulty airbag inflators.

Industry observers note that the pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles. Late-model Hondas make up over 810,000 units in the recall, while Toyota accounts for 790,000 units, 314,000 of which are located in the United States. NHTSA documents indicate that 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX, 2013 Acura RDX models, 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 ‌IS250, ⁠2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models are included in the recall.

It has been revealed that despite the growing recall population, the core matter remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls. “The airbag inflator propellant can degrade with repeated exposure to high-humidity environments and large temperature variation, resulting in increased internal pressure. If an affected airbag deploys, the increased internal pressure may cause the inflator to rupture (break apart) and deploy abnormally,” NHTSA documents explain. “In the event of an inflator rupture, metal fragments could pass through the airbag cushion material possibly causing serious injury or fatality to vehicle occupants.”.

It has been revealed that there have been no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being newly recalled. However, NHTSA has recorded 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009. The Takata airbag recall remains the largest recall in U.S. history.

Given the rolling nature of the Takata recall, Honda and Toyota were already in discussions with federal regulators when this airbag version began to show signs of degradation. Honda first identified an problem during simulation testing under severe environmental conditions in May 2025. However, these tests didn’t show abnormal inflator behavior or a “statistically significant deviation” from previous prediction models. Similarly, Toyota had been collecting and studying certain Takata inflators since 2016, specifically focusing on a desiccated, phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate (PSAN) propellant. Toyota’s predictive models indicated that some of these inflators could be reaching the end of their life, prompting the Japanese automaker to conduct a voluntary safety recall.

The remedy is fairly simple for both automakers: Toyota and Honda will simply replace the airbag inflators on affected units. Honda says its new inflators are manufactured by a different supplier and use a different propellant that does not degrade over the long term when exposed to high temperatures, high humidity, and large temperature fluctuations. Either way, both automakers and federal regulators urge affected owners to have their airbag inflators swapped out as soon as possible.

Hyundai is reportedly getting ready to pull the wraps off an all-new Porter pickup. This time, it’s electric.

Distinct from the Piaggio-branded Porter pickup that’s already sold in Europe, the Hyundai Porter is a conceptually similar, work-focused vehicle with a dropside pickup “bed” trailing a box-like passenger cab and a serious, professional-grade payload capacity.

Carscoops recently published photos of a heavily camouflaged Hyundai Porter prototype last month, along with claims that Hyundai means to follow up the success of sister brand Kia’s multifunctional PV5 electric vans with a globally available electric version of the truck as early as next year. This week, the wraps came off, giving us our best look yet at what the truck might look like when it makes its official debut.

In a recent development, after feeding as many spy shots as I could into some AI models, we ended up with the images you see here. If they’re accurate, they show a commercial-ready EV that’s meant to attract new fleet buyers looking to ditch diesel in Western markets while serving as a direct, 1:1 replacement for domestic fleet operators already putting Porter pickups to work.

It has been revealed that those operators will probably feel a little safer behind the wheel of the upcoming truck, too. Hyundai has worked a short hood and crash structure into the bodywork where a conventional “flat” cabover now sits – a move that seems to point both to a commitment to provide better front-end protection to the truck’s occupants and an intent to at least take an honest run at the Euro NCAP crash standards.

Beyond that, we don’t really know anything about the upcoming Korean pickup – but it’s a safe bet that the next-generation Porter will benefit from some of the technology that’s been baked into the Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP.S commercial vehicle platform that underpins the Kia PV vehicles. Those ship with 51.5 and 71.2 kWh battery options sending electrons to 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors, and while that’s far from a guarantee, it’s not nothing, either.

In a recent development, that’s my take, anyway – what’s yours? Will the Hyundai Porter EV make its way to the West on an AWD version of the E-GMP.S platform, or will it remain a regional model running on one of the manufacturer’s hybrid platforms? Let us know in the comments.

#133690. Tech Report: Every Choice Is a Loss: Why We Often Regret Lives Not Lived

Tech Report: Every Choice Is a Loss: Why We Often Regret Lives Not Lived

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Nurses often recount stories of patients near the end of their lives who express regrets about experiences they never had and paths they never took.
  • Sources indicate that in the first part of Either/Or, Søren Kierkegaard—writing through the persona of a young man, "A"—posits that life is inherently characterized by boredom and that the choices we make are attempts to escape this state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Nurses often recount stories of patients near the end of their lives who express regrets about experiences they never had and paths they never took. They sometimes wonder whether choosing differently might have made them more satisfied with their lives. Regret is, to some extent, part of almost everyone's life. If we marry, we may eventually regret it; if we do not, we may remain alone and regret that too. If we emigrate, we may regret leaving; if we stay and endure our circumstances, we may regret that as well. Whether we remain in a tedious job or choose another, whether we speak our minds to those around us or keep silent, we may still end up regretting our choices.

Sources indicate that in the first part of Either/Or, Søren Kierkegaard—writing through the persona of a young man, "A"—posits that life is inherently characterized by boredom and that the choices we make are attempts to escape this state. We choose things that promise pleasure, yet such choices never lead to lasting joy or satisfaction; what is thrilling today may become mundane and tedious by tomorrow. Boredom inevitably returns, leaving us to lament the choices we made and wish we had chosen differently. To break this cycle of regret and boredom, "A" offers an intriguing proposal: much like farmers who rotate crops to prevent soil erosion, individuals should constantly alter their approach to life—avoiding fixation on any single experience—in order to mitigate boredom. Praising the character of Don Juan—the seductive, womanizing figure from Mozart’s opera—"A" champions the rejection of all commitments as a means to banish boredom and regret. In the same volume, Kierkegaard introduces another character, Johannes, who employs psychological tactics to seduce a young woman named Cordelia, gradually cultivating her affection. He uses strategies such as maintaining distance, employing silence, sowing doubt, and stirring the other person’s emotions—all of which he finds deeply pleasurable.

In the second part, Kierkegaard writes through another persona, Judge Wilhelm. He recommends that “A” choose an ethical and committed life. A significant portion of this section addresses marriage. Wilhelm argues that only a stable, committed relationship can prevent the initial fire of love and passion from rapidly burning out, allowing it instead to endure. Through Wilhelm's voice, Kierkegaard writes that our choices shape our ultimate selves—an idea later further developed within existentialist philosophy. By employing pseudonymous characters, Kierkegaard deliberately avoids taking sides, leaving the conclusion to the reader. Ultimately, he presents choice and regret as fundamental components of human existence [1].

It has been revealed that now, we explore the neurological mechanisms underlying the persistent human experience of regret. In their book The Molecule of More, Lieberman and Long discuss two brain circuits—the mesolimbic and the mesocortical—both of which utilize dopamine as a neurotransmitter. The first circuit primarily drives "wanting," motivation, and the anticipation of a reward; it is not about the pleasure itself but rather the anticipated pleasure expected from a given stimulus. The second circuit activates top-down pathways for impulse control, enabling consideration of the future consequences of one's decisions and desires. From an evolutionary perspective, this capacity has allowed humans to transcend immediate, relatively simple responses and proposal for the attainment of long-term goals. However, this simplified model of the reward system’s neurology suggests that repetition of a stimulus leads to a diminished reward—driven by a decline in dopamine levels and function within the mesolimbic system—thereby shifting attention and motivation toward new rewards [2].

Although the prefrontal cortex is primarily responsible for logical reasoning, evaluation, and behavioral regulation, certain regions within it also play a role in generating feelings of regret. A 2004 study revealed that individuals with damage to the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), unlike healthy controls, did not report experiencing regret or anticipating negative outcomes during a gambling task. Additionally, other brain areas, such as the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the hippocampus, contribute to the experience of regret by enabling the mental simulation of alternative, unlived scenarios [3].

In an intriguing paper published in Science Advances in 2023, researchers examined the distinct roles of the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), the ventral striatum, and dopaminergic neurons in counterfactual thinking in monkeys. Their findings indicated that the brain can represent not only the reward actually received but also the value of a reward that could have been obtained through a different choice [4]. This suggests that, at times, the source of our regret is not an event that actually occurred in real life, but rather an event that never took place, yet one whose possibility the mind has retained. In effect, we may find ourselves mourning a life we ​​never lived.

In a recent development, in conclusion, the human brain is designed to anticipate the future outcomes of decisions we might have made and to compare those potential results with our current situation. While this capacity can aid in making better future choices, it can also foster a chronic sense of regret. This trait leads us to constantly evaluate our present circumstances against hypothetical alternatives—lamenting the paths we did not take. In the modern era, this inclination has been exacerbated by the rise of social media, which offers numerous opportunities for social comparison and exposes us to constant reminders of "alternative" lives. Observing the lives, homes, cities, and joys of others can trigger anxiety that we are perpetually falling behind.

Here, it helps to distinguish this phenomenon into two types: 1) Constructive Regret, which helps us recognize past mistakes and make better decisions moving forward; and 2) Ruminative Regret, which traps individuals in a cycle of constantly comparing their actual lives with hypothetical scenarios or the lives of others—without necessarily leading to any constructive action or decision. Since it is impossible to experience every life possibility or to know for certain whether a different choice would have been better, we can take the message of the second part of Either/Or to heart: By committing fully to our own lives, rather than constantly dwelling on lost possibilities, we can liberate ourselves from the anxiety and the wearying melancholy of regret.

In a recent development, 1. Kierkegaard, S., Hannay, A., & Eremita, V. (2004). Either/Or: A Fragment of Life. Penguin Books Limited.

2. Lieberman, D. Z. and M. E. Long (2018). The Molecule of More: How a Single Chemical in Your Brain Drives Love, Sex, and Creativity--and Will Determine the Fate of the Human Race, BenBella Books.

In a recent development, 3. Camille N, Coricelli G, Sallet J, Pradat-Diehl P, Duhamel JR, Sirigu A. The involvement of the orbitofrontal cortex in the experience of regret. Science. 2004 May 21;304(5674):1167-70.

4. Yun M, Nejime M, Kawai T, Kunimatsu J, Yamada H, Kim HR, Matsumoto M. Distinct roles of the orbitofrontal cortex, ventral striatum, and dopamine neurons in counterfactual thinking of decision outcomes. Sci Adv. 2023 Aug 9;9(32):eadh2831.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG.
  • This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.
  • Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios states the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

Sources indicate that as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

Sources indicate that so far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

The Thrilling Movies of David Fincher, Ranked From Alien 3 to The Killer

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, FOR MORE THAN 30 years, David Fincher has been making some of the coolest movies out there.
  • Recent findings suggest that after his 2020 film Mank—which tells the story of Citizen Kane screenwriter Herman J.
  • Sources indicate that his latest film—which will mark his last in a long relationship with Netflix—is kind of a special occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, FOR MORE THAN 30 years, David Fincher has been making some of the coolest movies out there. The 61-year-old director's work over four different decades includes the likes of Se7en, Fight Club, The Social Network, Gone Girl, and, now, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth; these are movies that know how to create a very specific style of tension that feels unique to a singularly talented visual storyteller, but are also entertaining thrillers that always have something to say. To put it simply, Fincher's films are often imitated, but never replicated.

Recent findings suggest that after his 2020 film Mank—which tells the story of Citizen Kane screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz and his eventual blackballing from Hollywood for political reasons—got something of a tepid response (by David Fincher standards, at least), the director returned in 2023 with a movie far more in tune with what he's best known for in The Killer, which starred Michael Fassbender as a chilling contract killer who lives his life by a code in a world increasingly dominated by consumerism.

Sources indicate that his latest film—which will mark his last in a long relationship with Netflix—is kind of a special occasion. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is a kind of sequel to Once Upon a Time... In Hollywood, reuniting Fincher with his most frequent leading man (in Brad Pitt) and allowing Pitt to reprise the character that won him his first Oscar for acting. There’s also the fact that the film features a script written by Quentin Tarantino, one that the Pulp Fiction director had originally planned to direct himself before his self-imposed ‘10 Films’ proposal led him to abandon the project before Pitt and Fincher helped to revive it. (Fincher becomes the fourth person to direct a Tarantino script, joining a list that includes only Oliver Stone, Tony Scott, and Tarantino himself.).

In a recent development, the movie shifts Tarantino’s bright, psychedelic ‘60s vibe of Hollywood for a darker, grittier one in the ‘70s that feels in line with Fincher’s whole thing. This is kind of a hangout movie, kind of a fixer movie, and kind of a neo-noir; it’s also a deeper exploration of Booth’s character and a real showcase for both Elizabeth Debicki and Scott Caan as a pair of newly introduced characters in show business.

Industry observers note that these are the kinds of conflicting, overlapping themes always present in Fincher's films, and part of what makes them so compelling. Fight Club, for example, is a satire on the kind of toxic masculinity that tends to make some people out there, well, the worst people in the world. Fincher himself has said that it's not his fault that some people tend to take the movie the wrong way, and we tend to land on his side. Time to work on that media literacy, clones.

We'd be remiss, too, to not talk about one of the collaborations that makes Fincher's more recent work pop so much: the presence of composers Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross. The Nine Inch Nails founder and his longtime collaborator have reinvented themselves in the past decade-plus as a constant presence in the industry, and their synths and tones make all of their work pop—but it feels especially right when paired with the visuals and performances that Mr. Fincher brings to the screen. That One Scene in Gone Girl (you know the one) is made even more memorable because of the music playing underneath, and the score for The Social Network is one of the best albums of the last 20 years.

That's enough for now, though. As you get ready for The Killer—or if you want to dive into Fincher's work all over again—we've got a complete ranking of all 13 feature films he's made in his impressive career.

Industry observers note that well, it’s no substantial surprise what’s at the bottom. Fincher has loudly disowned Alien 3, considered by many to be a low-point in an otherwise enjoyable franchise. To Fincher’s credit, it was his directorial debut and one where he was arguably set up to fail. As Ridley Scott was unavailable, the Alien 3 team cycled through multiple scripts and directors in a frantic attempt to recreate the success of the previous films. While Alien 3 has in more recent years been reconsidered by some fans to be at least a decent entry in the franchise, it’s without a doubt a notable stain on Fincher’s otherwise solid filmography. –Milan Polk.

The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008).

In a recent development, loosely based on an F. Scott Fitzgerald short story, The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a strange film to say the least. While the Oscar-winning film had great visual effects for its time, the film ultimately falls flat. While many great films have spawned from short stories, it’s clear that this particular story didn’t necessarily require more examination. It’s a hard sell to craft a thrilling romance out of the tragic and horrific tale of a constantly de-aging man. While at the time the film earned critical acclaim, it probably isn’t worth a rewatch. –MP.

Industry observers note that jodie Foster and Kristen Stewart as a mother and daughter duo? Sign us up. Panic Room is a solid thriller about a mother fighting for survival when three robbers come to steal the previous homeowners' bonds. It’s a perfectly watchable movie, but it’s not Fincher’s best. Released in 2002, Fincher was on a hot streak, coming off of Se7en, The Game, and Fight Club. After showing audiences some of his best work to date, it’s no wonder Panic Room didn’t land as strongly with its standard home invasion tale. Still, if anyone can make a decent thriller amongst his more well-known works, it’s David Fincher. –MP.

According to recent reports, mindhunter fans may have strong thoughts about Mank, which directed Fincher’s attention away from his Netflix series (although Fincher has mentioned audience numbers and his own heavy involvement, which ultimately took a toll on him, were factors in its end). That said, Fincher’s first Netflix feature film was a passion project for the director, whose own father wrote a screenplay for the movie. While the film garnered 10 Oscar nominations–winning Best Production Design and Best Cinematography–it’s overall less compelling than Fincher’s other works. –MP.

According to recent reports, the Game isn't the most iconic Michael Douglas movie of the '90s—that honor probably goes to Basic Instinct. The Game isn't the most iconic David Fincher movie of the '90s either—well, just keep reading the rest of this list for a few more of those. But you know what The Game is? A damn fine movie, a thriller with a plot filled with twists that will keep you guessing and compelling from the very start to the final frame. The movie may actually border on a twist or two too many, but that's a critique we're happy to deal with. —Evan Romano.

It has been revealed that fincher's latest finds the director returning to his roots—tense thriller—in an entirely fresh way. Michael Fassbender plays the titular character in a story that's both intentionally dry and has something real to say about the ever-present state of consumerism in modern times—even for a methodical master assassin. It might take a bit to get fully into The Killer's trance, but once it kicks in, the hypnosis is very real. —ER.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth (2026).

This movie existing at all is the kind of thing that movie lovers used to dream up as part of games invented to kill time. Fincher directing a script by Quentin Tarantino? Starring Brad Pitt? Like, yes please. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth has a story that feels like one of those pulp paperbacks you pick up before a long flight and can’t put down until you’re done (and given how much Tarantino has always loved the work of Elmore Leonard, that makes sense). It’s different from Once Upon a Time... In Hollywood, and that’s OK—the vibe is different, and it’s endlessly compelling. Elizabeth Debicki, who plays a character who may or may not have been the titular character of Tarantino’s original project, is a real standout here. In short? It’s just fun.

The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (2011).

Just like with Gone Girl (which we'll talk about a bit later), The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo proves that Mr. Fincher does well with turning popular books into a visual medium. Steig Larsson’s posthumously published Millenium series found critical acclaim worldwide, so it was only right a great director took on the gritty, dark adaptation. In creating the film, Fincher faced multiple obstacles, including: Sweden released its own trilogy of films in 2009, and the Millenium series entries are all door stopper novels. That’s not to mention the book’s depiction of graphic violence, likely to turn away some audiences. Despite it all, Fincher crafted a solid adaptation. Rooney Mara and Daniel Craig each give stellar performances as the two protagonists, and the film does well to recreate the book’s overall moodiness. The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo’s lower ranking isn’t due to its quality, but simply that Fincher’s filmography contains so much incredible work that they can’t all be in the top 5. –MP.

It has been revealed that for as big as the true crime genre has gotten in recent years, nothing has managed to top Zodiac, Fincher's 3-hour epic telling of the saga that surrounded the Bay Area's infamous Zodiac Killer. The cast, led by fantastic performances by Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, and Robert Downey Jr. (with great appearances from John Carroll Lynch and Brian Cox too), is actually only the second best part of the movie; the sense of constant dread that Fincher creates is both crushing for the viewer and extremely accurate to how it must have felt with one of American history's most horrific monsters on the loose. —ER.

Sources indicate that it's hard to find a movie more iconic than Fight Club. As one of many films released in 1999 to make a major cultural mark (think The Matrix, Being John Malkovich, The Sixth Sense, and The Blair Witch Project, among others), Fight Club is probably remembered most for its twist (which, if you somehow haven't seen the movie yet, we won't spoil here), and Brad Pitt's utterly unforgettable turn as Tyler Durden (along with an accordingly ripped body and stylish outfits). But even deeper here is a piece of work that puts Fincher's very best talents on full display: the movie is intense when it needs to be, very funny when it needs to be, and features some of the most memorable shots you'll see. Look folks, no one enters a room like Marla Singer. —ER.

Is Se7en a thriller? A mystery? A psychological horror? The answer to all of the above is a resounding Yes. All of the above. And it's absolutely masterful at all of it. After a rough experience on Alien³, Fincher hunkered down and made one of the all-time greatest movies of its kind. Led by a pair of commanding lead performances from Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman (as detectives investigating a series of grisly murders that seemingly follow a pattern inspired by the seven deadly sins), Se7en is dark, scary, and moody in a way that so many other movies in this world try to be—and can never quite pull off. —ER.

Recent findings suggest that as you can see, The Social Network is not the #1 movie on our list. But we'd be hard-pressed to say it's not the single most impressive in David Fincher's one-of-a-kind filmography. Here, Fincher manages to turn a story unlike any he'd done before—the story of the formation and early years of Facebook contains absolutely zero elements of the crime thrillers he's most known for—into one of the most compelling dramas you'll ever see, with stunning photography and characters you can't look away from. This may be the best (and, in a way, most vital) movie of the 2010s, and I genuinely sometimes lose sleep when I remember that Fincher didn't win the Oscar for Best Director. —ER.

Trust David Fincher to bring out the best performance in Ben Affleck’s entire film career (yeah, we’re calling it: it’s the best).

Sources indicate that as a major literary bestseller, Gone Girl was always going to be a thrilling movie adaptation. But with a director like Fincher, the film was not only a sensational thriller but an artistic work all on its own. It expertly captures the backdrop of post-recession millennial suburban malaise while chronicling a fascinating mystery. Rosamund Pike shines as the enigmatic and volatile Amy Dunne, rightfully earning herself a Best Actress nomination at the Academy Awards. Gone Girl is Fincher at his best, mixing his thriller skills with an astute exploration of contemporary culture, and a bit of his signature dark, dry, humor mixed in for good measure. If there’s any Fincher film that’s an absolute must-watch, it’s Gone Girl. –MP.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, so, you think you can run an electric car organization?
  • As first brought to our attention by Great Britain’s Car, Swedish auction organization Klaravik is preparing to sell the entire NEVS Emily GT project.
  • After Saab Automobile closed its doors in 2012 following an ill-fated tie-up with Spyker, a Chinese consortium called National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS) acquired the majority of the remaining assets, including the Trollhättan factory, manufacturing equipment and intellectual property.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, so, you think you can run an electric car organization? Well, here’s your chance to prove it. An entire electric vehicle development project is heading to auction this month, and it comes with almost everything you need to get started. There's even a connection to one of the automotive industry's most beloved defunct brands: Saab.

As first brought to our attention by Great Britain’s Car, Swedish auction organization Klaravik is preparing to sell the entire NEVS Emily GT project. The auction includes four complete prototype vehicles, a fifth development mule, spare body panels, parts, tools, and engineering drawings. And unlike a typical automotive auction, where you might leave with a single vehicle, the winning bidder gets the entire collection.

A little backstory is helpful here. After Saab Automobile closed its doors in 2012 following an ill-fated tie-up with Spyker, a Chinese consortium called National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS) acquired the majority of the remaining assets, including the Trollhättan factory, manufacturing equipment and intellectual property. However, NEVS was not interested in building a next-generation Saab 9-3 Aero. Instead, they had their sights set on building an electric car future.

In a recent development, their vision of that was called the Emily GT, envisioned as a sophisticated electric grand touring sedan capable of competing with established luxury EVs. Development began in late 2019, and just 10 months later, the Emily GT rolled out into view. And much like Saabs of the past, the Emily GT had some unique features—the most obvious being its four electric motors, one mounted inside each wheel. Combined, they produced a healthy 490 horsepower.

Recent findings suggest that however, while the power output was healthy, the financial condition of the company was not. NEVS never secured the funding necessary to bring the car into production. The ambitious project remained stuck in the prototype stage, where it’s stayed frozen .

Industry observers note that so, do you think you’re the right person to bring it to market? If so—or even if you’d rather just own a very odd automotive dead-end—Klaravik will open online bidding on November 25, with the auction scheduled to conclude December 9. All four completed vehicles and the accompanying development materials are being offered together rather than individually.

Of course, buying the prototypes and engineering materials doesn't automatically give someone a functioning car organization or guarantee a path to production. Manufacturing, regulatory approvals, and financing would still present enormous challenges. However, if you do happen to be an ambitious entrepreneur with deep pockets, this could be your chance to revive an electric vehicle that never had the chance to see the light of day.

Melissa Joan Hart Explains It All: Hot Flashes, Menopause, and Turning 50

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off.
  • Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline.
  • Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off. As a child, she didn’t understand why. Now, as a 50-year-old woman, Hart knows that her mom was experiencing hot flashes.

Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline. “I feel like it’s just becoming a hot topic with women, where…the taboo is going away from it now.”.

Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.

“[It] was really jarring, and the first few times, you’re not really sure what that was…do I need to turn the air down or what’s going on here?” Hart said.

Over time, she learned that she was experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, which affect up to 80% of women during the menopause transition and can persist for 7 to 10 years.

Doctors categorize hot flashes as mild, moderate, or severe, stated Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, at Corewell Health.

Industry observers note that “[So] if they’re mild, it’s a sense of warmth (maybe in the chest, or the neck, or the face). A moderate hot flash is where there’s associated sweating, and a severe hot flash is something that stops you in your tracks, wakes you up from the middle of the night,” Bitner told Healthline.

Hart has mostly experienced hot flashes while home or at her three sons’ activities, and they have yet to interfere with her work. However, according to research, one in three women report moderate to severe challenges in managing their work due to symptoms related to menopause.

In a recent development, “It’s just so sad that about 10% of women leave the workforce due to menopause,” mentioned Bitner. “And so it can really affect our ability to perform at these key years of not only institutional memory, but also of earning power, and it can really affect the whole community.”.

Bitner said women should feel empowered to bring up their menopausal symptoms or questions with their doctor.

“[This] is something that was taboo for so long…women didn’t really talk about this, whether it was because of embarrassment, or [they] weren’t sure if anyone was experiencing it,” she stated. “[There’s] no reason, in this day and age, we need to suffer through it…it’s something that there are treatment options for.”.

In fact, Bitner said providing specific details about their symptoms, such as how many mild, moderate, or severe hot flashes they’ve experienced over the past week, can help doctors better assess patients’ needs.

Hart looks to discuss treatment options for her hot flashes with her doctor soon. In the last few years, she remarked she has put emphasis on her midlife health.

“I just was sick of waking up with aches and pains in general [thinking], ‘is this the rest of my life?’” she noted.

She started listening to self-help books in the car while driving her kids around and found ways to put herself first.

“My kids are a little bit older, so I kind of have that freedom to be able to do that,” she stated. “[But] along with getting older, comes the menopause, comes that different time in life. And I think it’s a good time to reevaluate [how] our bodies can’t handle what [they] used to handle, and let’s figure it out.”.

Hart has partnered with pharmaceutical company Bayer on its “Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash” campaign, which encourages women to discuss menopause symptoms with their doctors and promotes Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription medication for moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause.

“It’s called ‘Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash’ campaign because it shouldn’t, because we should be able to push through, and this should be a time in our lives when our kids are getting older, and we’re able to kind of reinvent ourselves,” said Hart. “And I think it’s an exciting time, and it shouldn’t be something that we’re afraid of.”.

She is embracing speaking openly about midlife health.

“I hit 50 this year, and it was, like, a huge milestone, and I think that’s something to be proud of, and not something to shy away from,” she said.

Hart also hopes to challenge the longstanding barriers women face in Hollywood as they age, including fewer opportunities for leading roles.

“[I] think we’re seeing that the generation before, and my generation, it feels like we’re pushing those boundaries…and we’re saying, you know, that women at this age have a lot to give, have a lot of information to share, have a lot of stories to tell and experiences and adventures still ahead of us, and, you know, we’re not ready to stop,” Hart said.

In everyday life, Bitner mentioned that while some patients avoid talking about midlife complications like menopause with their doctors, she is seeing more patients who are confident being forthcoming.

In a recent development, as more women talk openly about menopause, she hopes to include men in the conversation, too. In fact, she invites her patients to bring their partners to appointments, so they can gain an understanding of menopause and the experiences their partners face, such as hot flashes, sleep concerns, vaginal dryness, and discomfort or pain during intercourse.

Sources indicate that “[Often], there’s, you know, comments that come up [from men who] say, ‘How do I talk about this without getting in trouble?’” said Bitner. “[We] want everyone to join this conversation…it doesn’t have to be just her issue because we know it’s not.”.

#133681. I Didn't Get the “Letting Go” Memo

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1000 w)
